uncited: The core mechanism modifies the radiance field function $F_\Theta$ to map input coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ to a tuple $(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, where $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a feature vector [12995-feature-fields.md].
The rendering of these features follows the same volume integration principle as color.
where $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ is the accumulated transmittance and $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ is the opacity weight [12995-feature-fields.md].

Supervision is performed by comparing the rendered feature $\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r)$ against ground-truth 2D feature maps or teacher network outputs projected onto the image plane [12995-feature-fields.md].
This process lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation [12995-feature-fields.md].
**Parameters:** $H$: Predefined maximum number of solid objects the network predicts.
**Pitfall:** Variable number of objects and large non-occupied volumes.
Augment sampled features with variance from multiple views to describe occupancy.

**Formula:** Density and latent features are computed as: $\sigma(\mathbf{p}), \hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}) = \text{G-MLP}(\bar{V}(\mathbf{p}), \gamma(\mathbf{p}))$, where $\bar{V}(\mathbf{p})$ is ray features aggregated and augmented from multi-view features, and $\gamma(\mathbf{p})$ is position encoding.

This directly supports every part of the claim.
